newsitem.title: UK: LME copper turned back from $2,280 in pre-market.
newsitem.headline: LME copper turned back from $2,280 in pre-market.

text.p: LME copper tried to break through $2,280 resistance in Thursday pre-market activity, leading the others slightly higher, but met stiff resistance, dealers said.
"It appeared to be some American houses trying to trigger stops above $2,280," one senior dealer said.
Three month prices popped up to $2,282, compared to an afternoon kerb close of $2,262 on Wednesday, but were turned back and later settled at $2,270/75.
The market was expecting a decline in stocks on Friday, the trader added.
LME inventories rose on Tuesday by 4,725 tonnes.
"That's bolstering the price...good buying should be seen on dips below $1,620. But there's heavy overhead resistance at $1,634/40," he added.
Zinc had a go at the upside in pre-market activity, peaking at $1,154 before easing back to $1,147, only $3 weaker than Wednesday's kerb close.
The market has been displaying technical overbought signals for several days but has remained resilient near recent highs.
"There are signs that prices may be reaching a plateau for now. Good support is provided by a short-term uptrend at $1,138/40," broker Brandeis said in a commentary.
Spreads flared again as the first tight dates, January 29/30, approach, with the premium of cash over three months firmer at $265/72 from about $250/$260 on Wednesday evening.
"We've heard that some of it has been pushed forward about a week, but we'll just have to wait to see whether the shorts cover," a dealer said.
Aluminium was indicated at $1,627/29, little changed from Wednesday's kerb close of $1,630.
Large falls in LME stocks were expected on Friday or possibly spread over the next two sessions, a dealer said.
